items.title: Ferrand Clementin Interview, 1973-08-02
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions 'watch Trump' in the context of funeral traditions, but the INTERVIEWEE only responds with 'Mm-hm' and does not claim a personal relationship or direct interaction with Trump.

ctx.x: It's old enough. When I was a kid, he'd play that for the funeral. He'd play that for the funeral when they send water. Oh, we're on the shoreline right here. Oh, it's not here. Oh, I knew it. I mean, at the funeral, do you used to play that? Sure. Do they play fast or slow? Oh no, they're just creeping along. They're creeping along. Mm-hmm. So it means slow? Yeah, slow. Oh, like that. How slow is that? Then after that, after that, they play that fast. I see. They used to play slow and then after they need the…

After all, how they call that man? Again, they used to be the most likely that I see that and remind me about him. His, uh, great brother, Bama. Oh yeah, Bama. I saw the reminder about the dead man they call Bama. Oh, every funeral in town they had him to watch Trump and then. He had a big, uh, what you call, uh, that thing was found, that wall. Full of flowers, all kind of the sand. And he had to hang on the side and he just got a flag. Exactly. And the way that man used to watch everybody, I was going to see…
